summary: Multi-head attention in Vision Transformers (ViTs) allows independent attention patterns across heads, but without explicit regularization, heads may learn redundant patterns rather than complementary roles. Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples.
takeaways: Our analysis shows that ViT-HarDis reduces the similarity of hard samples to competing class centers while decreasing inter-head attention similarity, and that applying disentanglement only to the final transformer layers outperforms regularizing the entire network.
Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples.
In face recognition (FR), hard samples whose embeddings lie close to competing identities are critical for optimization and generalization.
